boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Richmond traditions spanning first-year welcome, coordinate-college milestones, and commencement reflection.

cards.title: Enter through Investiture
cards.subtitle: First-year Richmond College welcome
cards.notes: Attend the formal welcome, hear the College’s history, and notice how the ceremony links a new class to earlier Richmond College classes.
cards.short_summary: A matriculation-style ceremony that formally welcomes first-year Richmond College students.
cards.evidence_claim: Richmond College describes Investiture as its formal introduction of first-year students and says the ceremony began with Dean Emeritus Richard Mateer.
cards.access_notes: University ceremony for the entering Richmond College class; confirm current event details with Richmond College.

cards.title: Sign the Honor Pledge
cards.subtitle: An Investiture ritual
cards.notes: Read the pledge before signing and use the moment to connect academic integrity with the student-run Honor System’s everyday expectations.
cards.short_summary: First-year students recite and sign the Honor Pledge as part of Investiture.
cards.evidence_claim: Richmond College states that first-year students recited and signed the Honor Pledge during Investiture.
cards.access_notes: Part of the first-year Investiture program; the Honor System is student-run.

cards.title: Receive the Class Coin
cards.subtitle: A unique design for each entering class
cards.notes: Keep an eye out for the class-specific design and save the coin as a tangible marker of the class’s entry into Richmond College.
cards.short_summary: Each entering Richmond College class receives a coin with its own design.
cards.evidence_claim: Richmond College says each first-year student receives a uniquely designed class coin, a tradition begun with the Class of 2015.
cards.access_notes: Presented to members of the entering first-year class during Investiture.

cards.title: Meet the Class Flag
cards.subtitle: Chosen by the first-year class
cards.notes: Look for the new flag at Investiture, then visit Whitehurst Living Room to see how current classes’ flags remain on display.
cards.short_summary: Each first-year class votes on a flag that follows it through Richmond College.
cards.evidence_claim: Richmond College says first-year classes vote on their flag; current flags are displayed in Whitehurst Living Room and retired at Culmination.
cards.access_notes: The flag is presented at Investiture; current class flags are displayed in Whitehurst Living Room.

cards.title: Pass Beneath Retired Flags
cards.subtitle: The close of Investiture
cards.notes: At Investiture’s conclusion, walk beneath the arch of retired class flags and notice the ceremony’s visual link between new and past classes.
cards.short_summary: New students leave Investiture beneath an arch made from retired class flags.
cards.evidence_claim: Richmond College reports that the entering class proceeds from Investiture under an arch of retired class flags representing earlier classes.
cards.access_notes: A ceremonial element at the conclusion of Investiture.

cards.title: Mark Richmond College Day
cards.subtitle: First week of March
cards.notes: Watch for the early-March celebration and use it to connect the present campus with Richmond College’s March 4, 1840 founding.
cards.short_summary: An annual birthday observance for the institution originally established as Richmond College.
cards.evidence_claim: Richmond College says this first-week-of-March celebration marks the university’s March 4, 1840 founding; it began in 1940 and was revitalized in 2014.
cards.access_notes: Held during the first week of March; consult Richmond College for the current year’s program.

cards.title: Close with Culmination
cards.subtitle: Senior Richmond College celebration
cards.notes: Join the senior reflection and look for the insignia pin presented for Commencement, along with the class flag’s retirement from display.
cards.short_summary: A formal Richmond College conclusion for seniors preparing for Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Richmond College describes Culmination as the formal conclusion for seniors; its elements include reflection, fellowship, a gift, and an insignia pin for Commencement.
cards.access_notes: For graduating Richmond College seniors; timing and participation details vary by year.

cards.title: Gather at Candlelight
cards.subtitle: Westhampton Lake, night before Commencement
cards.notes: If you are graduating, plan for the lake-side gathering and its student remarks; bring attention to the class’s final shared pre-graduation moment.
cards.short_summary: Graduates gather with candles on Westhampton Lake’s banks the night before Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Richmond identifies Candlelight Ceremony as one of its longest-standing traditions and says graduates gather with candles at Westhampton Lake at 10 p.m. the night before Commencement.
cards.source_title: Commencement traditions offer a chance to celebrate and reflect
cards.access_notes: For graduating students on the night before Commencement; confirm the current ceremony schedule and weather plan.

cards.title: Write to Your Senior Self
cards.subtitle: A Proclamation tradition
cards.notes: Write and seal the letter with a future reading in mind, then keep the sealed message for the senior-year Proclamation moment.
cards.short_summary: Westhampton students write a sealed letter to their future selves and reopen it as seniors.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Richmond Magazine calls Proclamation a Westhampton College tradition and identifies writing, sealing, and later opening a letter to one’s future self as integral to it.
cards.access_notes: Part of Westhampton College Proclamation; contact the Westhampton College Dean’s Office for current-year details.

cards.title: Process at Ring Dance
cards.subtitle: Junior Westhampton College celebration
cards.notes: If participating, follow the procession schedule, invite up to two companions if desired, and decide independently whether to order a University ring.
cards.short_summary: Junior Westhampton College students are individually recognized in a formal Ring Dance procession.
cards.evidence_claim: Westhampton College describes Ring Dance as a junior-class celebration of students’ academic and personal progress, with each participating student individually recognized in procession.
cards.access_notes: The current Ring Dance page lists ticketed entry and optional University or Westhampton rings; verify the class-year date, venue, and ticket requirements.
